Sources. Star positions and proper motions: van Leeuwen (2007), the Hipparcos new reduction (CDS I/311); for two stars (HIP 55203 and HIP 78727), Hoffleit and Warren (1991), the Bright Star Catalogue, 5th revised edition (CDS V/50). Johnson V and B−V: ESA (1997), The Hipparcos and Tycho Catalogues, ESA SP-1200 (CDS I/239). Credit: ESA. Used under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 IGO licence, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/3.0/igo/; ESA does not endorse this page. Names: traditional star and constellation names; star names as spelled in the Catalog of Star Names of the IAU Working Group on Star Names (the archival IAU-CSN, updated 2022-04-04, https://www.iau.org/public/themes/naming_stars/); other traditional star names from R. H. Allen (1899), Star-Names and Their Meanings (G. E. Stechert; https://archive.org/details/starnamesandthe00allegoog); for a star without a name, its Bayer or Flamsteed designation from the Bright Star Catalogue (CDS V/50), identified through CDS I/239, or else its Hipparcos number (HIP, CDS I/239); M6 and M7 by their Messier numbers; NGC 869, NGC 884 and NGC 6441 as CDS SIMBAD gives them. Constellation names in Norwegian, Spanish, French, German, Chinese and Japanese: Store norske leksikon (Rolf Stabell, Maria Hammerstrøm and Are Vidar Boie Hansen); VADEMECUM REMER, Glosario de astronomía y astrofísica (EA1URO mirror); Astronotas, Catálogo Messier; Xavier Nègre, Lexilogos; Sternregister-Team, Die 88 Sternbilder; Sun Guoyou, 天体收藏家; National Astronomical Observatory of Japan, 暦計算室; Chinese Academy of Sciences, National Astronomical Observatories, 天文学名词; Wikipedia contributors, Argo Navis (Spanish revision 172375908); and Allen (1899) for Argo in French and German. Where a language has no sourced form, the English name is shown. Identifications of Ptolemy’s stars: Verbunt and van Gent (2012), A&A 544, A31. The centres of Praesepe, M6, M7 and Coma Berenices (Melotte 111): CDS SIMBAD, from 2021A&A...647A..19T. These and the other clusters’ centres are held as static ICRS anchors; an integrated V is shown only where one is catalogued. All are selected and reformatted for this page.

Figure lines follow the plates of Urania’s Mirror, or a View of the Heavens (Samuel Leigh, London, [1825]), as held by the Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division (its rights statement: “No known restrictions on publication in the U.S.”), read from the unretouched scans mirrored on Wikimedia Commons; cards 10, 12, 15, 20, 28, 29 and 32 from photographs by the Bodleian Libraries, University of Oxford (Games 9(1), 1825), with thanks; Eridanus’s river on card 29 from the scan of John Dolby’s private set on Wikimedia Commons (marked public domain). The lines record only which stars each plate joins: no image of any plate is shipped, and the Bodleian’s photographs (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0) are not reproduced. Where a plate draws no segment, lines come from d3-celestial (Olaf Frohn), commit 7e720a3, under its licence, below.
